sanity_expectations: omega1(t), omega2(t), omega3(t) remain finite and real over t in [0,30]
Kinetic energy 0.5*(I1*omega1**2 + I2*omega2**2 + I3*omega3**2) is monotonically non-increasing (drag dissipative)
Angular-momentum magnitude sqrt((I1*omega1)**2 + (I2*omega2)**2 + (I3*omega3)**2) is monotonically non-increasing (dissipative drag; no applied torque)
Intermediate-axis instability: starting near the omega2 (I2, middle inertia) axis, amplitude leaks into omega1 and omega3 (tumbling) before drag damps the state toward zero
All three angular velocities approach zero as t -> 30 (drag dominates the long-time behavior)
domega1_dt at t=0 approximately equals ((I2-I3)*omega2*omega3)/I1 = (2-3)*4*0.1/1 = -0.4 (Euler coupling dominates initially; drag corrections are O(0.01))
excitation_report: Full child-vs-parent ODE-system comparison on the target trajectory: new-term peak effect on domega1_dt = 0.6402 (128.0x sigma=0.005), strongest at t≈2.11 where intermediate-axis tumbling swaps omega1<->omega2 amplitude so the misalignment-rotated linear/quadratic drag becomes visible. Domain-term scales: Euler coupling (I2-I3)*omega2*omega3/I1 ~ O(0.4-1.6) during tumbling (>>5*sigma); linear anisotropic-drag term ~ O(0.01-0.05) (>=5*sigma once mixing engages); quadratic anisotropic-drag term ~ O(0.02-0.15). All terms above 5*sigma at some point in t in [0,30].
role_corrections: domega1_dt: O->O (confirmed, target derivative of the state omega1)
rotational_drag_axis_misalignment_angle: P->P (confirmed, pi/6 ~ 0.5236, within suggested [-pi/4, pi/4])
rationale: Inherit the ODE-system contract verbatim. Distinct principal inertias I1=1, I2=2, I3=3 with omega2-axis initial spin trigger intermediate-axis instability, exposing omega1<->omega2 exchange that makes the newly-introduced misalignment-rotated drag terms visible (new-term = 128x sigma per excitation_check). Misalignment angle = pi/6 (within suggested [-pi/4, pi/4], nonzero to activate the rotation mixing). Anisotropy strengths 0.5 keep all effective drag prefactors positive (1+alpha*(3Ii/sumI-1) stays positive for both alpha=0.5 since (3Ii/sumI - 1) in [-1, 0.5] here). Drag coefficients 0.05 (linear) and 0.02 (quadratic) are mild vs the O(1) Euler coupling. t in [0,30] covers a few tumbling cycles plus damping decay. sigma=0.005 is ~1% of the peak Euler term and ~0.8% of the new-term peak, so it's a strict yardstick without swamping small features.
